text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- President Jacques Chirac to attend 50th anniversary of CNPF employers' federation today.
-- Alcatel Alsthom and Lagardere Groupe expected to put in bids today for electronics group Thomson SA with the French Treasury.
-- In an interview, former budget minister Nicolas Sarkozy calls for greater tax cuts, easing of France's monetary policy.
-- Company heads expect exports to boost activity but see stagnant investment and domestic demand, poll finds.

-- Budget deficit for 1997, to be announced on Wednesday, may be similar to the 288 billion-franc deficit announced for 1996 in light of planned cuts in income tax. Total public deficit is expected to remain under the three percent of GDP set by Maastricht Treaty criteria, due to funds owed by France Telecom to the state.
-- CNPF employers' federation calls for an eight-billion-franc cut in unemployment payroll contributions.

-- Generale des Eaux chairman Jean-Marie Messier confirms he expects his group to return to profit in 1996, seeks to become largest French private telecommunications operator, competing with France Telecom.
-- European agriculture ministers to tackle EU agriculture support schemes today, as cereal prices soar.
-- Leaders of Bosnia and Serbia to meet in Paris within three weeks to discuss the future of Bosnia after Saturday's vote.
